documents.content:
# Project Atlas - Architecture Update (Q3)

Author: Priya Nair (Principal Engineer, Platform Team)

## Summary

Project Atlas is our new enterprise knowledge platform. Over the last quarter the Platform Team migrated Atlas from a monolithic Django service to a set of Python microservices. Priya Nair led the migration together with Marcus Feld, who owns the data ingestion service.

## Key Technology Decisions

We adopted Neo4j as the primary graph store for Atlas because our access patterns are relationship-heavy. We use the neo4j Python driver for all data access. For semantic search we standardised on SentenceTransformers embeddings stored directly in Neo4j vector indexes.

The team also introduced LangChain to orchestrate the retrieval-augmented generation pipeline. Marcus Feld prototyped the extraction service using the LLMGraphTransformer component.

## Decision Log

Decision D-114: Adopt Neo4j as the system of record for the knowledge graph. This decision affects Project Atlas directly and supersedes the earlier PostgreSQL proposal.

Decision D-118: Use SentenceTransformers for embeddings in the near term to avoid external API dependencies, revisiting OpenAI embeddings once the budget is approved. This affects Project Atlas.

documents.content:
From: Priya Nair <priya.nair@example-corp.com>
To: engineering-all@example-corp.com
Subject: Project Atlas Beta is Live

Hi everyone,

I am thrilled to announce that Project Atlas has entered beta. The Platform Team has been working on this for two quarters and it is finally ready for internal users.

Atlas is built on Neo4j and uses LangChain for its Graph RAG pipeline. Marcus Feld and Diana Okoro drove the ingestion and retrieval work respectively. Diana Okoro is our resident expert in Python and SentenceTransformers, and she tuned the vector search layer.

The Data Platform Team owns Project Atlas going forward. If you want to contribute, Marcus Feld is coordinating onboarding.

Thanks to everyone involved.

Best,
Priya

documents.name: ATLAS-231_ingestion_timeout.txt
documents.content:
Issue: ATLAS-231
Title: Ingestion pipeline times out on large PDF batches
Severity: High
Status: Open
Reporter: Diana Okoro
Assignee: Marcus Feld

Description:
The Atlas ingestion pipeline times out when processing PDF batches larger than 500 documents. The bottleneck appears to be synchronous embedding generation with SentenceTransformers before writes to Neo4j.

Impact:
This issue blocks Project Atlas from reaching general availability, since enterprise customers routinely upload thousands of PDFs. The Data Platform Team has flagged it as a launch blocker.

Proposed fix:
Batch the embedding calls and write to Neo4j asynchronously. Marcus Feld is investigating a queue-based approach.
